claims.status_note: #1 and #4 state the need, #3 names countries where communities are wanted, and #6 gives examples of regional communities growing. Nobody in the thread argued against it; #4 notes that some past ZCG candidates floated cutting regional budgets but says they are not the majority.
claims.text: More capacity is needed in regional teams and community outreach, because regional communities are closest to end users and Zcash needs an active presence in more countries.

claims.status_note: #4 agrees the two-wing proposal is not needed at this moment because ZCG's performance has been good, #5 welcomes that agreement, and #7 concludes no new ZCG wing is needed after #6. Nobody argued for adding a committee now; #4's separate point about a possible wing is claim c8.
claims.text: Extra resources should go to the people doing the work, not to another permanent ZCG committee or a two-wing structure, which does not scale productive capacity.

claims.status_note: #1 cites ZCG's 11th May minutes; #3 and #6 describe the same progression and add Zcash Mexico, Zcash Nigeria and Zcash Africa as examples. Nobody disputed it.
claims.text: The route ZCG -> ZecHub -> new Ambassadors and emerging communities already exists and works: new communities start with ZecHub, build a track record, then get direct ZCG funding once established (e.g. Zcash Brazil, Zcash en Español).

claims.status_note: #1 gives the dates and says ZCG called the decision purely financial; #6 independently describes the program being discontinued and ZecHub taking it over. Nobody disputed it.
claims.text: The original Global Ambassador Program was suspended in January 2024 for financial reasons, after which ZecHub took the work over and Ambassador activity ran through the ZecHub DAO.

claims.status_note: Stated in #1 with the figures; nobody confirmed or disputed them.
claims.text: ZecHub's 2026 grant cut the Ambassador allocation to 20% of the bounty fund (20 ZEC) from 40% (400 ZEC) in 2025, a budget cut even though ZEC rose in USD terms.

claims.status_note: #5, #14 and #17 agree more funding is needed, and #7 asks whether ZecHub has enough funding and capacity; nobody argued against it, though #4 raises the unpaid-DAO workload point (c10) and #5 softens 'ring-fenced' as too fixed.
claims.text: Ambassador and emerging-community work needs enough dedicated funding, such as a larger ZCG allocation administered through ZecHub, rather than a small slice of ZecHub's general bounty fund that competes with other priorities.

claims.status_note: #1, #6 and #12 each name specific people who progressed from the program, and #14 confirms; nobody disputed it.
claims.text: The Global Ambassador Program also worked as a pipeline for future community leaders: Artkor now sits on ZCG, and Yoditar, Chidi, Michael2xl and AidenZ went on to build communities and take broader roles.

claims.status_note: #4 floats it while saying the two wings are not needed right now. #1, #5 and #7 argue that capacity should come from funding the doers, not another ZCG committee; #4 did not reply further.
claims.text: A dedicated community-grants wing of ZCG, backed by a ZIP, could be one way to ensure funding for regional communities keeps flowing.

claims.status_note: Made in #4 and #6; nobody responded to the point.
claims.text: Local context matters: something that seems unnecessary in one region may be useful in another, outreach cannot be done the same way everywhere, and regional community members would add value by running for ZCG.

claims.status_note: Raised in #4. #5 replies that it does not intend ZecHub to take the main flow, only incubation, but accepts that DAO workload and compensation would need review if its role grows; no one disputed the point itself.
claims.text: ZecHub DAO members (23 of them) are, as far as the author knows, unpaid, so if the DAO took the main flow of community grants with a much larger budget they would need to commit more time and take on more responsibility.

claims.status_note: Reported from experience in #8; #9 calls the figures a useful benchmark but nobody checked or disputed them.
claims.text: A simple model (easy-start resources, small ZEC support after an event or two, a support person, a private ambassador chat, a resource hub, a group directory) established over 100 in-person groups in about 30 countries for roughly $30k, and was the highest-ROI activity.

claims.status_note: Proposed in #8 and echoed in #9, #10 and #15. #9 asked @yoditar whether it fits the ZecHub model; #18 does not address that question.
claims.text: The practical meetup layer (the meetzec toolkit and group directory, with the ZecHub wiki holding reusable resources) fits alongside the ZecHub incubation model, and ZecHub could take it over or pull its data via an API.

claims.status_note: Raised in #9; #11 agrees and says any information kept should be public anyway. Nobody described the actual data handling.
claims.text: Because meetzec involves people and location or contact data, what is collected and retained and the site's security controls need care; ideally only public information about groups is kept.

claims.status_note: Proposed in #12 and endorsed in #14; nobody argued against it.
claims.text: Rather than recreating old programmes exactly, the community should learn from what worked and what did not, and be intentional about recognizing, mentoring and growing emerging leaders, with funding that matches each stage.

claims.status_note: Announced in #16 with discussion moved to a separate thread; #18 says it is being reviewed, and #20 says three alternative approaches have surfaced there. Nothing in this thread weighs it.
claims.text: A temporary (test) ZecHub sub-DAO for incubating community projects should be tried, as set out in a separate draft proposal.

mind_changes.note: Accepts the DAO workload and compensation concern from #4 for the case where ZecHub's role grows; in the same post also takes the point that 'ring-fenced' may sound too fixed.
mind_changes.span: If that grows, then yes, DAO workload and compensation would need looking at too.

posts.annotation: Argues capacity should go to people doing the work via the existing ZCG -> ZecHub route, not new ZCG wings; cites history, a 2026 Ambassador budget cut, and proposes a larger funded allocation through ZecHub if it wants it.

signals.note: Agrees with the stated goal of more regional capacity before disagreeing about where it should live.
signals.span: But I am in full agreement that more capacity is needed in regional teams and community outreach.

posts.annotation: Invites several regional organisers to say what worked, what did not, and whether scaling the ZecHub model is the right next step.
Says ZecHub supports small communities until they grow and ZCG then funds them, as with Zcash Brazil and Zcash en Español, and wants active communities in more countries.

Says the two-wing proposal is not needed now, but a dedicated community wing backed by a ZIP could safeguard regional funding; values local context; notes ZecHub DAO members are unpaid, with 23 members versus a possible 3-5 person wing.

Agrees with the progression described, clarifies ZecHub would only handle incubation, accepts DAO workload and pay would need review if that grows, and says enough funding matters more than ring-fencing.

signals.note: Accepts the workload and compensation concern raised in #4 for the case where ZecHub's role grows.
signals.span: If that grows, then yes, DAO workload and compensation would need looking at too.

posts.annotation: Describes how community building grew from ECC, Foundation and ZCG's Global Ambassador Program to ZecHub, and gives Zcash Mexico and Zcash Africa as examples that the ZecHub-then-ZCG route works.
Concludes from #6 that the ZecHub incubation model exists and works so no new ZCG wing is needed, and asks whether ZecHub has enough funding and capacity for the incubation stage.
Reports that a simple group-building model established over 100 groups in about 30 countries for around $30k, describes the toolkit they are building (meetzec), and offers to support ZecHub.

signals.note: States their past role running the Bitcoin Cash Association.
signals.span: I founded and ran the Bitcoin Cash Association a number of years ago

signals.note: Says they are already building the meetup toolkit described in the post.
signals.span: I've already started the process to try and offer as much of this as possible.

posts.annotation: Calls the meetup toolkit the practical side of the incubation model and the 100 groups for about $30k a benchmark, urges caution about data collected by meetzec, and asks others if it fits the ZecHub model.
Suggests making more use of the wiki and creating an events resource page.
Agrees about information storage and says any information retained should be public group information, communicated through an existing channel.
Argues the Global Ambassador Program also created a pipeline of community leaders, and suggests being intentional about recognizing and mentoring such leaders rather than simply recreating it.
Praises #1 and says improving what already exists would be good.
Agrees with #12 that the program was also a path to bigger roles, wants to learn from what worked and did not, and wants a clearer path from early activity to established work with matching funding.
Suggests meetzec for the practical meetup layer and the ZecHub Wiki for the reusable resources behind it.
Announces a draft proposal for a temporary ZecHub sub-DAO for incubating community projects, with discussion in a separate thread.
Says more funding to support more ambassadors and communities would be good, because the program is growing.

open_questions.text: Does ZecHub have enough funding and capacity to run the incubation stage properly, particularly if more communities come through it?
Does ZecHub want to take on the incubation role, and would the practical meetup layer fit its model?
Would ZecHub DAO members need compensation or more time if the DAO's role grows?
What information should meetzec collect and retain, and what security controls should protect it?
How do the draft ZecHub sub-DAO proposal and the three alternative approaches compare?

overview.text: vaspholdings opens by answering the two-wings idea from the June ZCG election thread. They agree more regional capacity is needed but would put resources into people doing the work through the existing ZCG -> ZecHub -> new Ambassadors route, citing ZCG's minutes, the Global Ambassador Program's 2024 suspension, and ZecHub's reduced 2026 Ambassador allocation. They suggest a larger ZCG allocation administered through ZecHub, if ZecHub wants it, and invite regional organisers to weigh in.

gordonesTV and yoditar describe the same progression working in practice (Zcash Brazil, Zcash en Español, Zcash Mexico, Zcash Nigeria). palmar agrees the two-wing proposal is not needed right now, though a dedicated community wing backed by a ZIP could safeguard regional funding, and warns that ZecHub's unpaid DAO members would need more time and responsibility if it took the main flow of grants. vaspholdings clarifies only incubation is meant, accepts the workload point, and concludes no new wing is needed.

zcashminer1 adds experience building a global network of in-person groups for the Bitcoin Cash Association and describes the meetzec toolkit. vaspholdings treats it as the practical layer of the incubation model while cautioning about people and location data; zcashminer1 agrees that retained information should be public; Dre_Nesthub proposes using the wiki; and vaspholdings suggests meetzec for meetup tooling and the wiki for resources.

Sewa recaps the Global Ambassador Program's history, noting it also produced community leaders, and asks the community to be more intentional about recognizing and mentoring them; Dpeluola and vaspholdings agree. vaspholdings then announces a draft proposal for a temporary ZecHub sub-DAO, with discussion moved elsewhere, yoditar says more funding would help the growing program, and vaspholdings notes three alternative approaches have surfaced.

positions.label: Scale the ZCG -> ZecHub route; no new ZCG wing or committee
positions.summary: The model of ZecHub incubating new Ambassadors and communities, then ZCG funding them directly, already works. Extra capacity should be funding for people doing the work, administered through ZecHub if it wants the role, rather than another permanent ZCG committee.

positions.label: Wings not needed now, but a community wing could safeguard funding
positions.summary: ZCG's performance has been good, so the two-wing proposal is not needed at the moment. A dedicated community-grants wing backed by a ZIP could still ensure regional funding continues, and ZecHub's unpaid DAO members would need more time or compensation if it took on the main grant flow.

positions.label: Add a practical meetup toolkit and resource layer
positions.summary: Make starting an in-person group easy with resources, small support after events, a contact person and a directory. meetzec can supply meetup tooling and the ZecHub wiki the reusable resources, with caution about the data collected.

positions.label: Learn from the Ambassador history and grow leaders
positions.summary: The Global Ambassador Program also grew future community leaders. The community should learn from what worked and failed, recognize and mentor emerging leaders, and build a clear path from early activity to established, funded work.

summary.tldr: Thread asks how to fund new Zcash Ambassadors and emerging regional communities. vaspholdings argues for scaling the existing ZCG-to-ZecHub route rather than adding ZCG wings; regional organisers agree the route works, with open points on ZecHub's funding and capacity, DAO workload, and a meetup toolkit.
